statement: The native Layer-N judge-qualification gate was not met by any evaluated judge configuration. Per owner directive 2026-07-11 this is recorded as a Layer-N INSTRUMENT invalidity PENDING an offline static (no-live-call) code review, and explicitly NOT as a judge-capability verdict. The same three judge configurations passed the harder, adversarially-audited Layer-O (Stage-Q v3) instrument (all three QUALIFIED).

judges.note: PARTIAL — run stopped mid-judge on owner directive; same trajectory (all 7 clean controls it reached were flagged, composites 15.0-38.6)

falsePositiveRate.meaning: every one of the 9 clean-control items was flagged

perClassSensitivity.observed: 0.000 on ~6/8 defect classes for both completed judges; NO class reached the 0.70 minimum

failureSignature.interpretation: flag-everything (FPR 1.0) + detect-no-planted-defect (sensitivity ~0) is the signature of an instrument/corpus problem, not a capability gap. A capability failure would show low sensitivity WITH low FPR (misses defects and does not over-flag).

rootCause.summary: The Layer-N corpus fixtures are sub-shippable-quality stubs, and the gate uses the real reader-review SHIP bar as the flag signal; therefore every fixture (clean or defective) is flagged on general quality, making clean-control specificity impossible and anchored defect-detection unreachable.
mechanism: The real phase-1 reader-review instrument (reviewOneChapter) ships a chapter only at composite >= AUTHOR_CHAPTER_BAR = 80.

The 43 Layer-N fixtures render to 248-2186 bytes (median 801) — thin stubs, not full chapters. A real reader-quality review scores them 12.7-47.9/100, all far below 80, so review.pass=false on EVERY item.
scoreJudgeQualification counts a clean control as a false positive when (valid && !pass). With pass=false on all clean controls, falsePositiveRate = 9/9 = 1.000.

Defect detection requires a complaint to anchor-match the planted mustQuote quote. Real complaints are about the chapter being an underdeveloped stub, not the specific planted defect, so anchorMatched=false and detected~=0 (sensitivity ~0).

validateQualCorpus checks only structural properties (mustQuote anchors are byte-substrings of the rendered doc, all 8 classes present, >=2 clean controls). It never verifies that clean controls actually PASS the real instrument, so the corpus is structurally valid but semantically un-passable by any real judge.
evidencePointers: LAYER-N-FAILURE-EVIDENCE.json (per-judge metrics, clean-control composites, fixture sizes)
fixtures/rendered/*.phase1.txt (the exact docs each judge read)

preserved: all completed and partial per-item reads (100)
per-spawn route sidecars + manifest/result records under logs/exec (token-free; verified)
two completed judge qualification.json + the partial third judge's per-item artifacts
sealed schedule, spec, thresholds copy, and run manifest

pendingStaticReview.type: offline, read-only, NO live model calls

mustDetermineIntendedPurposeOfLayerN.A: qualify FULL shippable-chapter review (then fixtures must be ~80+ quality chapters carrying planted defects)
mustDetermineIntendedPurposeOfLayerN.B: qualify TARGETED defect detection (then the gate must not use the ship/pass bar as the flag/detection signal)
mustDetermineIntendedPurposeOfLayerN.C: test a capability DISTINCT from Layer-O (then that capability must be defined and the instrument built to it)

ledger.note: ceiling is a hard maximum, not a target; no further live calls until the static review completes

relationToPriorInstrumentClassifications: Distinct instrument from Stage-Q. Stage-Q v1/v2 were STAGE_Q_INSTRUMENT_INVALID (Layer-O). This is the FIRST Layer-N invalidity. The owner's Stage-Q §11 final-stop rule governed Layer-O v3 (final Stage-Q); it does not by itself decide Layer-N.
